instruction:
Please act as a professional Verilog designer. Your task is to create a Verilog module that implements a touch sensor interface. 
The touch sensor can be either capacitive or resistive and the module should be able to handle both types of sensors. 
The touch sensor interface should have the following inputs and outputs:

Inputs: a trigger signal (trigger), a mode signal (mode), and a sensor signal (sensor)
Outputs: a touch detection signal (touch)

The trigger signal is used to initiate a touch detection cycle. The mode signal is used to select between capacitive and resistive sensors. 
The sensor signal is the input from the touch sensor, which will be either a capacitance or a resistance value depending on the selected mode. 
The touch detection signal should be high when a touch is detected and low otherwise.

To implement the touch sensor interface, you should first use Verilog code to define the capacitance and resistance values as functions of the sensor signal. 
Next, you should use these functions to determine whether a touch has been detected. For capacitive sensors, a touch is detected when the capacitance value exceeds a certain threshold. 
For resistive sensors, a touch is detected when the resistance value falls below a certain threshold. 
Finally, you should use the trigger and mode signals to control the touch detection cycle and select the appropriate sensor mode.
